fields.label: Contract Template Help
fields.options:
Writing Contract Terms

Each Terms row is a Jinja template. Reference the contract’s fields directly by their fieldname — no doc. prefix:

Contract value: {{ "{:,.0f}".format(net_total) }} {{ frappe_icon("saudi-riyal") }}
Customer: {{ customer_name }} — Date: {{ frappe.utils.formatdate(start_date) }}

Helpers

  • {{ frappe.utils.in_words(net_total) }} — amount in words.
  • {{ frappe.utils.formatdate(start_date) }} — date in the user’s locale.
  • {{ "{:,.0f}".format(net_total) }} — number with thousands separators.

Icons

Use frappe_icon("<name>") to inline any Frappe (Lucide) icon by its name. It renders in both the form preview and the PDF and follows the surrounding text colour. Optional arguments: size and color.

Saudi Riyal symbol : {{ frappe_icon("saudi-riyal") }}
Bigger, grey       : {{ frappe_icon("calendar", size="1.2em", color="#444") }}

Find icon names in the Lucide gallery (e.g. saudi-riyal, calendar, user, check).

Pulling data from a linked document

Link fields such as sales_order hold only a name. Fetch the document to read its fields:

{% if sales_order %}
{% set so = frappe.get_doc("Sales Order", sales_order) %}
Sales Order: {{ so.name }} — {{ frappe.utils.formatdate(so.transaction_date) }}
{% endif %}

How rendering works

The Terms fields are Code (Jinja) fields — they store your template verbatim and are never auto-rendered. This template is copied raw into each contract (where it stays editable), and is rendered only at print time by the Print Format. Nothing is rendered on save.

Showing the terms in a Print Format

In your Print Format’s Custom HTML, loop the contract’s terms and render each row:

{% for row in doc.contract_terms %}
{{ frappe.render_template(row.terms_and_conditions_primary, doc.as_dict()) | safe }}
{% endfor %}

Use row.terms_and_conditions_foreign for the foreign-language column. | safe outputs the HTML instead of escaping it.

Finding fieldnames

See every available field via Customize Form > ERP Contract.

Templating

Templates use the Jinja templating language. Read the Jinja documentation.
